resolution: Model import (.obj/.glb) was OOM-crashing V8: the import pipeline allocated a boxed JS object per byte (base64ToBytes number[]), per vertex/index (readAccessor number[][]), and a string-keyed weld map, so a 9-14MB scan/sculpt (100k-1M+ tris) blew the ~1.4GB heap; the partial EditMesh also overflowed the 4MB localstore value (BufferTooSmall). Rewrote importMesh.ts to parse into a flat typed-array MeshSoup (Uint8Array base64, Float32Array positions, TextDecoder JSON, two-pass objToSoup) that never explodes the heap, added decimateSoup vertex-clustering as a Detail knob plus gridForTargetTris seeding and a soupToEditMesh budget guard (MAX_IMPORT_TRIS=25k) that throws cleanly instead of crashing. The live studiokit ImportModelDialog now parses on Choose and shows a Detail slider with a live 'source N tris -> import M tris' readout, decimating before building the EditMesh and disabling Import when over budget (default ~12k). 11/11 importMesh unit tests pass; full hmsc-int cart bundles clean. Hot-reload picks up the TSX/TS automatically. Decimation is coarse vertex-clustering (cheap, can upgrade to QEM later); raising the 4MB localstore ceiling / storing big models outside editor-state is a possible follow-up.
